To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conjugate vaccine approach is a promising approach for smoking cessation.

1) Nicotine conjugate vaccines can be used to induce anti-nicotine antibody titers in mice; 2) These antibodies can block nicotine from binding to its receptor in vitro and can prevent nicotine from inducing nicotine-mediated behaviors in vivo; and 3) The antibodies can prevent nicotine from binding to the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor in vivo, and can prevent nicotine-induced behaviors in mice.
Nicotine conjugate vaccines are a promising new treatment for nicotine addiction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a nicotine conjugate vaccine as a novel approach in smoking prevention and cessation.
the development of a novel approach in smoking abstinence, namely the use of nicotine conjugate vaccines (NCVs).
the development of a novel nicotine vaccine for the treatment of smoking cessation.

the current pharmacological treatments for smoking cessation are not effective for the majority of smokers.
